title: Read through a pad
hints: Padding is a mask, not memory. Some logical positions have no buffer element behind them at all.
Turn the logical position into a buffer position first: `i = j - left`. Then decide whether `i` is a real element.
Only `0 <= i < n` may read `row[i]`. Every other position returns 0 without touching memory, because the bytes on either side belong to someone else.
explain: The reference computes `i = j - left` and reads `row[i]` only when `0 <= i && i < n`, returning 0 otherwise. The check comes before the read, so the padded positions never touch the -1 sentinels around the row.
